title: Nondisclosure Agreement — Adams County Regional Water District and an unnamed "Company", executed 2024-01-10

provenance.evidence: Native text layer (PrimoPDF export of the executed copy, /Title "NONDISCLOSURE AGREEMENT"). The form is captioned "Nondisclosure Agreement (1/14)" on p.1 and "(10/13)" on p.2 — two revision stamps of the drafter's own template on one instrument, recorded as read.

parties.agency: ADAMS COUNTY REGIONAL WATER DISTRICT ("Agency") — a regional water district organized under R.C. Ch. 6119, 9203 SR 136 / P.O. Box 427, West Union, OH 45693. Signed by Rickey W. Adamson, General Manager, 1/10/2024. [verified] — the AGENCY box of the executed page is complete.
parties.company: ⚠️ NOT NAMED ANYWHERE IN THE INSTRUMENT. [verified] as an ABSENCE, read off the document: the recital reads "A company (together with its Affiliates or agents of any of the foregoing, collectively the 'Company') has approached you in connection with a project that may be located in _______" — the location blank is unfilled — and the notice block reads "Notices to Company will be delivered: Attn: [____________________]."
parties.company_identification_mechanism: §Preamble and the closing notice paragraph together make the anonymity a designed feature, not an oversight: "When the Company has revealed its identity to the Agency, all references to the 'Company' in this nondisclosure agreement will be deemed to be (a) references to the Company's actual legal entity ... and (b) CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION", and "The Company may change the foregoing notice information at any time and expects to provide new contact information ONCE IT HAS REVEALED ITS IDENTITY TO THE AGENCY."

board_action.body: Board of Trustees, Adams County Regional Water District
board_action.motion_verbatim: "to approve permission for Rick Adamson to sign a non-disclosure agreement for a company interested in purchasing and developing the former Stuart Generating Plant land"

authorization.sequence_note: ⚠️ THE SIGNATURE PRECEDES THE AUTHORIZATION BY ONE DAY. The executed page is dated 1/10/2024; the Board voted 2024-01-11. [verified] from two independent primary sources (the instrument's own agency box and the District's own minutes). This corpus records the discrepancy and does NOT resolve it — a one-day gap is equally consistent with a clerical date, a ratification practice, or a signature ahead of authority, and nothing in the corpus distinguishes them. ⚠️ Do not characterize it as unauthorized signing.

terms.statement_verbatim: "'Confidential Information' means all nonpublic information ... relating to Company or disclosed by Company or its Affiliates to Agency ... including THE NATURE, CONTENT, AND EXISTENCE OF THE PARTIES' COMMERCIAL RELATIONSHIP or discussions about a possible relationship or transaction, or any discussions or negotiations between the parties."
terms.note: The existence of the relationship is itself the secret. This is the clause that makes the District's own minutes read "the company" for two years.

terms.statement_verbatim: "Agency may disclose Confidential Information as required to comply with (a) orders of governmental entities with jurisdiction over it and (b) applicable freedom of information or public records laws, IF Agency (i) gives Company PRIOR WRITTEN NOTICE sufficient to allow Company to seek a protective order or other remedy ..., (ii) discloses only such information as is required by the governmental entity, and (iii) uses commercially reasonable efforts to obtain confidential treatment for any Confidential Information so disclosed."
terms.note: A private notice-and-object window bolted onto R.C. 149.43. ⚠️ It fixes NO number of days, unlike the five business days in Sidney's CRA §32 (data/extracted/sidney/). Whether such a clause is enforceable against Ohio's public-records act is a legal question this corpus does not answer; what is [verified] is that a public body agreed to it.

terms.statement_verbatim: "This Agreement is effective as of the date Confidential Information is first received and will continue for 3 years, after which it AUTOMATICALLY RENEWS unless either party terminates ... by providing at least 90 days prior written notice ..., provided, that Agency's obligations with respect to Confidential Information will survive for 5 years following termination ..., and Sections 6, 9, 10, and 11 will survive INDEFINITELY and the confidentiality obligations ... will continue to apply ... for as long as the information continues to constitute a trade secret."
"This Agreement will be governed by internal laws of THE STATE IN WHICH THE PROPERTY WHERE THE PROJECT IS TO BE BUILT IS LOCATED, without reference to its choice of law rules."
terms.note: Drafted to be signed before the site is known — the same posture as the unfilled location blank in the recital. [inference] that this is a multi-state siting template; nothing in the instrument says so.

terms.statement_verbatim: The executed copy carries a completed AGENCY box only. No Company signature, printed name, title, date or notice address appears anywhere on either page.

open_questions.question: Who is the "Company"? The corpus cannot answer from this instrument. The 2024-01-11 minutes describe it only as "a company interested in purchasing and developing the former Stuart Generating Plant land". By 2024-10-10 the District's minutes call the project "Project Galaxy"; by 2025-10-09 they retire that name. Buck Canyon Properties, LLC appears on the District's own plan set (route parcel #30, auditor parcel 1830000070002) and on the USACE jurisdictional determination — but NO instrument in this corpus joins that LLC to this NDA.
Does a countersigned copy exist? R.C. 149.43 request to ACRWD for the fully executed agreement, any amendment, and any §5 notice the District has given or received.
Has §5 ever been invoked — i.e. has the District notified the Company of a pending public-records request? That correspondence would name the counterparty.

title: Consent Order (Adams County C.P. 89-CIV-228)
warnings: Article V milestone (c) prints "August 2, 1993" with a stray overstrike mark immediately right of the "2" — a typewriter correction or scan artifact. The digit "2" itself is unambiguous at 600 DPI and no second digit is legible, so the date is recorded as 1993-08-02; verify against the page image before citing the day in a filing.

Three values on the instrument are HANDWRITTEN, not typed: the day and month in the entry line ("Entered this 29th day of June, 1993", p. 7), the resolution number (p. 10) and the resolution date (p. 10). The entry date is corroborated by the clerk's MECHANICAL file stamp and is [verified]; the resolution number and date rest on the handwriting alone.

The Village Clerk's PRINTED name appears nowhere in the instrument — only a signature on p. 10. It is left null rather than transcribed from the hand. The Mayor's name is printed (p. 8) and is not affected.

fields.agency: Ohio Attorney General (Environmental Enforcement Section), for the State of Ohio
fields.respondent: The Village of West Union, Ohio
fields.facility: Village of West Union wastewater treatment plant and sanitary sewer system, Adams County, Ohio. The order does NOT print a plant address or name a receiving water.
fields.stipulated_penalties: Two schedules (Art. XI), both per day and PER VIOLATION, payable by certified check to "Treasurer, State of Ohio" within 10 days of the failure (Art. XI.C). For the CONSTRUCTION milestones, Art. V(a)-(f): $100/day up to 30 days, $200/day for 31-60, $300/day for 60-90, $400/day over 90. For the COMPLIANCE milestone, Art. V(g): $500/day up to 30 days, $750/day for 31-60, $1,000/day over 60 — a 2.5x-to-5x step up from the construction tiers.
fields.status: unresolved in corpus — the published bytes are a 1993 snapshot. The court expressly RETAINED jurisdiction to enforce (Art. XII) and the instrument contains no termination provision at all (unlike the 1996 Allen County CWA decree, which conditions termination on 12 consecutive compliant months). Nothing in the corpus shows whether the 1995 milestones were met or whether jurisdiction was ever released.
fields.summary: Entered and filed 1993-06-29 in the Adams County Court of Common Pleas (Judge Elmer Spencer) on the State's 1989 complaint, resolving alleged violations of the discharge limitations and monitoring requirements of NPDES permit 0PC00019*CD and of R.C. Chapter 6111. Three injunctions run together: immediate compliance with R.C. Ch. 6111 and the permit (Art. IV.A); Appendix "A" interim effluent limits until 1994-10-03 and the permit's final effluent standards after (Art. IV.B/C); and elimination of all sanitary-sewer overflows and bypasses plus completion of the WWTP improvements described in the Facilities Plan submitted to Ohio EPA on 1992-05-26, on a seven-milestone schedule ending 1995-05-01 (Art. V). $5,000 civil penalty, stipulated penalties on every milestone, and reporting to Ohio EPA's Southeast District Office within 7 days of each milestone date.

obligations.requirement: Initiation of Project Design Work (Art. V(a))
Submittal of Approvable Plans and Specifications to Ohio EPA (Art. V(b))
Completion of construction of sufficient wetstream treatment facilities to ensure compliance with final effluent limits, and to eliminate all bypasses and overflows from the system (Art. V(f))
Attain compliance with final effluent limitations (Art. V(g))
Comply with the Appendix "A" interim effluent limitations (Art. IV.B)
Meet the final effluent standards of NPDES 0PC00019*CD (Art. IV.C)
Written report to Ohio EPA Southeast District Office, Division of Water Pollution Control, 2195 Front Street, Logan, Ohio 43138, stating whether each milestone was performed (Art. VII)
obligations.deadline: 7 days from each milestone completion date

obligations.requirement: Pay the $5,000 civil penalty by certified check to "Treasurer, State of Ohio" (Art. X)
Properly operate and maintain the WWTP and any associated equipment and structures (Art. IV.D)
Provide a copy of the Consent Order to each contractor employed on the work, and require each general contractor to provide a copy to its subcontractors (Art. II)

fields.note: [verified] All figures, dates and codes read from the instrument's own page images. The order is entered "without trial of any issue of fact or law, and upon consent of the parties" (p. 1), so the State's characterization of the Village's conduct is an allegation the order RESOLVES, not a finding it makes — see `alleged_violations`. Compliance with the order's terms constitutes full satisfaction of civil liability for all claims alleged in the Complaint (Art. III.B), but does not limit the State as to claims not alleged, including violations occurring after the filing (Art. III.C).

title: Adams County Water Company, Inc. — member vote to amend the Articles of Incorporation, converting the corporation to a Chapter 6119 regional water district and renaming it the Adams County Regional Water District, Inc.

fields.instrument: Adams County Water Company, Inc. — member vote to amend the Articles of Incorporation, converting the corporation to a Chapter 6119 regional water district and renaming it the Adams County Regional Water District, Inc.
fields.body: Members (customers) of Adams County Water Company, Inc., in annual meeting

vote.motion_verbatim: "the amendment of the Articles of Incorporation to convert the corporation to a Chapter 6119 Regional Water Authority, to change the name of the corporation to Adams County Regional Water District, Inc."
vote.ballot_method: ballots/proxies, counted by inspectors appointed by the President

disclosures.statement_verbatim: "Richard Seaman, Jr., announced that the customers had approved, by a vote of 579 yes and 141 no, in favor of the amendment of the Articles of Incorporation to convert the corporation to a Chapter 6119 Regional Water Authority, to change the name of the corporation to Adams County Regional Water District, Inc."
disclosures.note: 80.4% in favor on 720 votes cast. What was traded is visible only by reading this document against the by-laws that followed: under the predecessor company the trustees were ELECTED by the members at this very meeting, by petition and ballot, with vote totals published. Under the 1994 by-laws the board "shall be composed as per the Entry of the Court", and vacancies are filled by a three-trustee nominating committee and a two-thirds vote OF THE TRUSTEES. ⚠️ Nothing in this corpus records what the members were told the conversion would mean for their franchise; the minutes report the result, not the campaign.

disclosures.statement_verbatim: "Richard Seaman, Jr., gave the results of the election as follows: Wendell Barnes - 390; Patrick Bihl - 334; Maggie E. Cooper - 332; Russell Gaffin - 324; James Lloyd - 409; Vernon 'Beau' Moore - 280. President Lloyd declared Wendell Barnes, Patrick Bihl, and James Lloyd duly elected. Attorney David Wilson swore in the Trustees and administered the oath of office."
disclosures.note: The last contested election in this corpus, held minutes before the vote that abolished the mechanism. Six candidates for three seats, published totals.

disclosures.statement_verbatim: "the company is planning, in conjunction with the Farmers Home Administration and the Appalachian Regional Commission, to construct line extensions in the following areas: Portsmouth Road, 12,866 feet; State Route 73, 21,000 feet; Frog Hollow, Hackelshin, and Black Hollow roads, 28,000 feet; and State Route 41 to Woodland Altars, 19,000 feet. The project will be funded with FmHA, ARC, and local funds. The total estimated cost of the project is $535,000."
disclosures.note: Context for scale: the whole 1993 capital program was $535,000 across 80,866 feet of main.

financials.operating_account_verbatim: "OPERATING ACCOUNT, consisting of cash on hand, certificates of deposit, money market deposit, Farmers Home Administration reserve, and Farmers Home Administration supervised construction account amounted to $1,001,643.76."
financials.note: ⚠️ The rendered page prints "$1,001.643.76" — a typewriter period where a comma belongs. Read as $1,001,643.76 from the digit grouping. Recorded because the corpus rule is that figures come from the image and the image is imperfect here.

fields.signature_note: ⚠️ The President's signature line reads "James Lloyd, President" but the signature above it is Wendell Barnes's. Recorded as read; not reconciled.

title: Adams County Regional Water District — Resolutions 97-19, 97-20, 97-119, 98-49 and 98-90: trustee appointment, re-appointment, and the definition of the term-expiration date

fields.body: Board of Trustees, Adams County Regional Water District
fields.meeting_date_note: Earliest of the set; the run spans 1997-02-13 → 1998-12-10 (see `acts` below).

mechanism.statement_verbatim: "In accordance with the By-Laws of the Board of Trustees of the Adams County Regional Water District, the President of said Board did appoint a nominating committee to nominate a successor to fill the unexpired term of Mr. Tadlock, and ... The Nominating Committee has recommended the appointment of Chris Baxla for the said term"
mechanism.note: The by-laws' vacancy mechanism (three-trustee nominating committee → two-thirds of the trustees) operating in fact. No court, no county appointing authority and no electorate appears anywhere in the chain.

acts.subject: Appointment of Chris Baxla to the unexpired term of Jimmy Tadlock, ending 1997-12-31

disclosure.statement_verbatim: "Jimmy Tadlock has submitted his resignation from the Board of Trustees of the Adams County Regional Water District due to A CONFLICT WITH HIS POSITION AS TOWNSHIP TRUSTEE"
disclosure.note: The one seat in this record vacated over an office-holding conflict, and it is the township-trustee seat. Recorded without inference about the nature of the conflict — the resolution does not state it.

acts.subject: Defining the trustee term-expiration date as December 31, to align with the District's fiscal year
Re-appointment of Chris Baxla, Gary McDowell and Sam Cooper for three-year terms ending 2000-12-31

conflict_handling.note: ⚠️ ALL THREE BENEFICIARIES VOTED ON THEIR OWN RE-APPOINTMENT — two by abstaining, and Cooper by voting NO on his own. The vote carried 5-1 on a nine-member board. Recorded as the record shows it; the abstentions are the board handling the conflict, not concealing it, and this corpus draws no adverse inference from a recusal.

acts.subject: Appointment of Daniel Fristoe to the unexpired term of Steve Ryan, ending 1999-12-31
acts.note: Ryan resigned "due to personal reasons". Fristoe was still a trustee at the 2024-01-11 meeting — a 26-year tenure beginning with an appointment, never an election.

acts.subject: Re-appointment of Russell Gaffin, Gerald Gray and Richard Seaman Jr. for three-year terms ending 2001-12-31

conflict_handling.note: The same pattern one year on: every beneficiary abstains, five trustees appoint three.

board_roster_1997_02_13.note: Transcribed from the roster table dated 1997-02-13 filed with Res. 97-19/97-20.
board_roster_1997_02_13.continuity_note: ⚠️ THREE OF THESE NINE WERE STILL SEATED IN THE 2024-2026 MINUTES — Howard A. "Tony" Staggs (by then President), Gerald Gray and Chris Baxla. With Daniel Fristoe (appointed 1998, trustee at the 2024-01-11 meeting), FOUR members of the board that authorized the Buck Canyon NDA had held their seats for a quarter century or more, none of them ever elected to it. [verified] by name against the committed 2024-2026 minutes. ⚠️ Tenure is a fact here, not a finding — long service on a rural utility board is unremarkable, and this corpus asserts no impropriety from it.

title: Adams County Regional Water District — Resolutions 26-41 through 26-47, adopted 2026-07-09

fields.instrument: Adams County Regional Water District — Resolutions 26-41 through 26-47, adopted 2026-07-09
fields.body: Board of Trustees, Adams County Regional Water District

present.visitors_note: "and a few others that did not sign the attendance register"

attendance_vs_tally.observation: ⚠️ EIGHT trustees are recorded present (Tolle absent), and every one of the seven resolutions below records the verbatim tally "Yes 7  No 0". The tallies are transcribed exactly as printed and are NOT reconciled or adjusted here.
attendance_vs_tally.what_the_document_itself_says: The minutes state the presiding-officer rule in their own words, on p.0 — "President Staggs stated the vote was seven to zero to terminate. AS THE PERSON LEADING THE MEETING ONLY VOTES IN CASE OF A TIE, the vote was unanimous with those eligible to vote." — and p.4 then prints a full roll call on the executive-session motions naming exactly seven voters: Brent Crawford, Lynn Weeks, Luke Rhonemus, David Tatman, Gerald Gray, Chris Baxla, Timothy Grooms. President Staggs does not appear in that roll.
attendance_vs_tally.note: Recorded because 8 present against a 7-vote tally is the kind of arithmetic a reader will check. No inference is required to explain it and none is made: the seven voters are NAMED on the page, and the rule that accounts for the eighth is QUOTED on the page. This entry adds no explanation the document does not supply, and asserts nothing about how any individual trustee voted on any resolution below — the roll call at p.4 covers the executive-session motions, not Resolutions 26-41 through 26-47, whose tallies are recorded only in aggregate.

disclosures.statement_verbatim: "Estimated Proprietary Funds: Unencumbered Cash on Hand $9,200,000; Revenues Received $5,700,000; Total $14,900,000. Estimated Expenditures: Operating Expenses $5,100,000; Debt Service $300,000; Capital Improvements $1,500,000; Total $6,900,000. Total Estimated Cash on Hand: 12/31/2027 $8,000,000."
disclosures.note: The Official Certificate of Estimated Resources and Expenditures for FY2027, signed 2026-07-09. Scale context for any claim about what this District can finance.

disclosures.statement_verbatim: Two executive sessions: "according to ORC 121.22 G (3) for possible litigation concerning a former employee issue", and "according to ORC 121.22 G (8) for confidential matters."
disclosures.note: Both roll calls recorded 7-0. ⚠️ The minutes record only the statutory purpose, never content. R.C. 121.22(G)(8) is the trade-secret/confidential-information exception — the same statutory family as the NDA's subject matter — but NOTHING in the minutes connects this session to the Buck Canyon project, and the corpus does not connect them. It is recorded because the (G)(8) invocation is itself a fact about how this board meets.

disclosures.statement_verbatim: "Roxie McNeilan addressed the Board protesting the termination of her husband, Kevin McNeilan. Attorney Grimes informed her that Ohio is an 'at will' state for employment. President Staggs stated the vote was seven to zero to terminate."
disclosures.note: Recorded as the meeting's own opening business. A personnel matter unconnected to the campus, carried because it is on the same page as the record above it and omitting it would misrepresent the meeting. No inference is drawn.

disclosures.statement_verbatim: "The Board stated that the 'Interim' could be removed from Johnny Hayslip's title to now become General Manager. His salary will be discussed at a later date."
disclosures.note: ⚠️ The District has a new General Manager. Rickey W. Adamson, who signed the 2024-01-10 NDA, no longer holds the office; the corpus does not record when or why he left it.
